notes: 3D road slabs and scenery silhouettes occupy the same ground; Y-fork trunks and mounds cross paved segments. The 2D dotted overlay continues through those crossings.
Large untextured polygonal scenery sits in front of the graph; a triangular mass covers a mystery node on the right. Node seats are repaired after scenery is placed and still lose.
Upper-right combat medallions sit close enough to read as a collision; spacing is a post-scenery repair with a capped shove rather than a shared layout.
Branching stone segments and 2D bezier dots cross and merge in the centre/upper-right so the next legal step is visually ambiguous.
Act II has no readable 3D pavement in this corpus; cold route state is a 1.7px dotted 2D overlay at low alpha on dark fog and is easy to lose.
PathBand and waystones are 2D children painted after MapScene so dotted edges and medallions draw through 3D scenery the road would otherwise disappear behind.
Canonical opening pose (DEFAULT_XZ) and zoom-0 do not compose the Vigil as a hero landmark; at focused zoom-3 it sits on the lower-left edge instead of reading as a terminus.
Act I focused zoom-3 packs nodes scenery and pavement with little rest; Acts II–III invert that into large empty fog versus a tight node cluster. No shared composition contract.
Act IV resolved 3 of 8 kits and kept black placeholder cones cubes and discs. Act I also stamps the same Y-fork / mound silhouettes along the road.
